Tuam
too'am
n. (the archbishopric of Connacht in the Irish-speaking west, the most remote of the four Irish provinces)
From Irish Tuaim, a burial mound or tumulus; the full name Tuaim da Ghualann, the mound of the two shoulders.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Tuam in County Galway was the metropolitan see of Connacht, the poorest and most thoroughly Irish-speaking of the four Irish provinces, where English was barely heard outside the garrisons. Christopher Bodkin held it from 1536 and conformed to every change of religion from Henry VIII to Elizabeth, keeping the see through all of them; the crown valued him because he could preach in Irish and because Connacht could not be governed from Dublin. The deeper problem at Tuam was never the archbishop's conformity but the want of Irish-speaking ministers and of Irish books: there was no printed Irish New Testament until 1602 and no Old Testament until 1685. The dictionary records the see because the promise about God's name runs from the sunrise to the sunset and does not stop at the edge of a language: “From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised” (Psa 113:3).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines metropolitan as belonging to a metropolis, an archbishop; a province as a country belonging to a kingdom, a district under a governor; and incense as perfume exhaled by fire, an offering.

expand to see more

METROPOLITAN, n. The bishop of a mother church; an archbishop who superintends the conduct of suffragan bishops.

PROVINCE, n. [L. provincia.] A country belonging to a kingdom or state, either by conquest or colonization; the district of an archbishop.

INCENSE, n. [L. incensum.] Perfume exhaled by fire; the odours of spices burnt in religious rites; acceptable prayers and praises.

PURE, a. [L. purus.] Separate from all heterogeneous matter; clear; free from moral defilement.

WEST, n. The point where the sun sets at the equinox; the region of the setting sun.

Key Scripture

Psa 113:3 — "From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised."

Mal 1:11 — "For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts."

Isa 59:19 — "So shall they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun. When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him."

Mat 8:11 — "And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

Modern Corruption

The archbishopric of Connacht in the Irish-speaking west, held from 1536 by Christopher Bodkin, who conformed to every change of religion from Henry VIII to Elizabeth.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The failure at Tuam is worth naming exactly, because it is usually described as Irish resistance and was at least as much English neglect. A crown that wanted Connacht reformed appointed archbishops, took the revenues, and did not fund Irish-speaking preachers or print Irish Scriptures for most of a century. The Reformation elsewhere spread by vernacular Bible and catechism within a decade; in Connacht the New Testament arrived in Irish sixty-five years after the break with Rome and the Old Testament a hundred and fifty. That is not a people refusing a book they were offered.

The principle to recover is that God's intention for his name is geographical and total, and the texts say so in the language of sunrise and sunset. The Psalm fixes no limit: “From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised” (Psa 113:3). Malachi promises worship among the Gentiles in every place, with a pure offering (Mal 1:11), and Isaiah has the fear of the LORD coming from the west as well as the east (Isa 59:19). The Lord himself says many will come from east and west to sit down in the kingdom (Mat 8:11).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mizrach (H4217), the sunrising; Hebrew mebo' (H3996), the going down or entrance.

expand to see more

Hebrew mizrach (H4217) — the place of sunrise, the east; Psalm 113:3.

Hebrew mebo' (H3996) — an entrance, the going down of the sun, the west; Psalm 113:3.

Hebrew halal (H1984) — to praise, to commend; “is to be praised”, Psalm 113:3.

Hebrew qetoreth (H7004) — incense, perfume; Malachi 1:11.

Hebrew ma'arab (H4628) — the west, the sunset; Isaiah 59:19.

Usage

"“From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised” (Psa 113:3) — the Irish-speaking metropolitan see of Connacht."

"“my name shall be great among the Gentiles” (Mal 1:11) — no printed Irish New Testament until 1602."

"“That many shall come from the east and west” (Mat 8:11) — and no Irish Old Testament until 1685."
